identity.name: Post-Consent OAuth Token Abuse — Salesforce Bulk API Mass Export with Query-Job Deletion (Bling Libra)
identity.summary: A stolen, already-trusted third-party Connected App token drives high-volume Salesforce Bulk API exports across Account/Contact/Case/Opportunity from an automation user-agent, then deletes the query jobs to erase evidence. There is no consent event, no MFA prompt, and no interactive login to alert on — only export volume, user-agent drift, and the export-then-erase sequence betray it.
identity.description: This CLOUD_APP scenario models the post-consent phase of the Salesloft Drift supply-chain campaign attributed to Bling Libra (ShinyHunters) and the Scattered Lapsus$ Hunters umbrella (SP1D3R HUNTERS / SLSH / 'Trinity of Chaos'). Between August 8-18, 2025 the actor used OAuth access/refresh tokens stolen from the Salesloft Drift integration to exfiltrate data from affected customers' Salesforce tenants. Because the token was already consented and trusted, the classic identity signals are absent: no new OAuth consent grant, no MFA challenge, no login-history anomaly. The tradecraft that IS observable is behavioral: (a) the token drives Salesforce Bulk API query jobs at a volume and object-diversity far above the integration's learned baseline (Account, Contact, Case, Opportunity), (b) the exfiltration client presents the automation user-agent 'Python/3.11 aiohttp/3.12.15' (an indicator published in the cited Unit 42 Salesloft Drift threat brief, which reports 'the user agent string Python/3.11 aiohttp/3.12.15 associated with these login events'), and (c) after the bulk pull the actor deletes the Bulk API query jobs to hide evidence of the queries they ran — an export-then-erase anti-forensics sequence a legitimate integration never performs. Source IPs in the Salesloft disclosure included Tor exit nodes, which are explicitly high-false-positive for orgs that permit Tor, so the exfil user-agent is treated as a corroborating (not standalone) IOC. A hand-authored BIOC keyed on a single bad object or SOQL string would miss this because every operation is a legitimate Bulk API call — which is exactly why the emphasis is ABIOC: two auto-tuned Analytics Behavioral IOCs anchor the deviation to the compromised integration identity's causality chain (trusted token -> high-volume CRM export -> query-job deletion), and a correlation rule fuses them into a single post-consent-token-abuse incident. Hunting substrate is Salesforce Event Monitoring (including UniqueQuery real-time events that log the executed SOQL), Connected App authentication activity, and login history, ingested into XSIAM.

campaigns: Salesloft Drift OAuth supply-chain data theft and extortion (Aug-Oct 2025)

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-CLOUD-006 — post-consent OAuth token abuse: Salesforce Bulk API mass export with query-job deletion (non-destructive signal-injection stand-in).

prerequisites.description: Salesforce Event Monitoring (incl. UniqueQuery real-time events) and Connected App authentication activity are ingested into XSIAM so Bulk API query/queryAll/deleteJob operations and the exfil user-agent are modeled and queryable.
prerequisites.check_command: echo 'confirm Salesforce Event Monitoring data source is connected to XSIAM'

prerequisites.description: A baseline window has elapsed during which the Connected App integration user ran only its scheduled, low-volume Bulk API jobs so Cortex learned the integration-identity export profile.

payload.code:
# NON-DESTRUCTIVE signal-injection stand-in — no real Salesforce data is read or
# deleted. curl reaches an AUTHORISED canary host; SAFE-MODE marker files stand in
# for the exported/erased query jobs so the export-then-erase behaviour is observable
# without touching real CRM records.
set -euo pipefail
API="https://${TARGET_HOST:-127.0.0.1}/services/data/v61.0"
EXFIL_UA="Python/3.11 aiohttp/3.12.15"
# (a) high-volume Bulk API export across the four CRM objects with the exfil UA
for OBJ in Account Contact Case Opportunity; do
  curl -s --max-time 5 -A "$EXFIL_UA" -X POST "$API/jobs/query" \
    -d "{\"operation\":\"query\",\"query\":\"SELECT Id FROM ${OBJ}\"}" -o /dev/null 2>/dev/null || true
  echo "SAFE-MODE export marker object=${OBJ} rows=250000 ua=${EXFIL_UA}" > "/tmp/sf-006-export-${OBJ}.marker"
done
# (b) export-then-erase: delete the Bulk API query jobs (anti-forensics)
for OBJ in Account Contact Case Opportunity; do
  curl -s --max-time 5 -A "$EXFIL_UA" -X DELETE "$API/jobs/query/750SIM${OBJ}" -o /dev/null 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -f "/tmp/sf-006-export-${OBJ}.marker"
done
echo '[CortexSim] SIM-CLOUD-006 post-consent Bulk API export-then-erase complete.'

input_variables.name: TARGET_HOST
input_variables.description: Authorised canary host that stands in for the Salesforce API endpoint the Bulk API export traffic reaches.

expected_artifacts.description: Outbound HTTPS Bulk API query-job requests carrying the automation exfil user-agent to the Salesforce API host.
High-volume Bulk API query/queryAll jobs across Account/Contact/Case/Opportunity followed by deleteJob operations issued by the same integration token.
SAFE-MODE export marker files recording the exported object names and row counts (no real CRM data), created then deleted to model the export-then-erase sequence.

iocs.context: Automation user-agent published in the cited Unit 42 Salesloft Drift threat brief ('the user agent string Python/3.11 aiohttp/3.12.15 associated with these login events'), presented by the high-volume Bulk API exfiltration client. High-signal but corroborating only — the same brief notes many source IPs in the Salesloft notification are Tor exit nodes with a high false-positive rate, so treat volume + export-then-erase as the primary anchor and this UA as confirmation.

abiocs.name: Post-Consent OAuth Token High-Volume Bulk API Export Deviating from Integration Baseline
abiocs.description: A Connected App integration identity whose learned Cortex baseline is low-volume, narrow-object, scheduled Bulk API activity suddenly drives high-volume query jobs across Account/Contact/Case/Opportunity from an automation user-agent. No consent, MFA, or login event exists to alert on; the ABIOC anchors the deviation (export volume + object diversity + user-agent) to the integration identity's learned baseline rather than to any known-bad object or SOQL string, catching post-consent token abuse a static rule would miss.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter cloud_service = "salesforce" and event_type = "BulkApi" and api_type = "Bulk"
| filter operation in ("query", "queryAll")
| filter object_name in ("Account", "Contact", "Case", "Opportunity")
| comp sum(rows_processed) as run_rows, count_distinct(object_name) as run_objects by connected_app, integration_user, user_agent
| join type = inner (dataset = cloud_audit_logs | filter cloud_service = "salesforce" and event_type = "BulkApi" and api_type = "Bulk" | filter operation in ("query", "queryAll") and _time < to_timestamp(current_time() - 3600) | comp avg(rows_processed) as baseline_avg_rows, max(rows_processed) as baseline_max_rows, count_distinct(object_name) as baseline_objects by connected_app) as base connected_app = base.connected_app
| filter run_rows >= (base.baseline_max_rows * 5) and run_objects > base.baseline_objects
| sort desc run_rows
| fields connected_app, integration_user, user_agent, run_rows, run_objects, base.baseline_max_rows, base.baseline_objects
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned integration-identity Bulk API baseline (low row volume, narrow object set, scheduled cadence, stable user-agent) -> trusted OAuth token reused -> high-volume multi-object export whose volume/diversity/user-agent diverge from the baseline, anchored to the originating Connected App + integration user.

abiocs.name: Export-Then-Erase Bulk API Query Job Deletion by Exfiltration Token
abiocs.description: The same integration identity that just ran a high-volume Bulk API query job then issues deleteJob on that SAME job_id within the same short window — a query-then-erase sequence keyed on job linkage and ordering (delete after query), not a bucketless co-occurrence. Deleting completed Bulk jobs is normal housekeeping for some ETL/backup integrations, so this does not fire on job deletion alone; it fires when a large export and the deletion of that same job happen in-window for an identity whose learned baseline is to leave its query jobs in place, anchored to the mass-export causality chain.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter cloud_service = "salesforce" and api_type = "Bulk"
| filter operation in ("query", "queryAll", "deleteJob")
| bin _time span = 30m
| comp count_distinct(operation) as op_kinds, sum(rows_processed) as exported_rows, min(if(operation in ("query", "queryAll"), _time, null)) as first_query_time, max(if(operation = "deleteJob", _time, null)) as last_delete_time by _time, connected_app, integration_user, user_agent, job_id
| filter op_kinds >= 2 and exported_rows >= 50000 and last_delete_time > first_query_time
| sort desc exported_rows
| fields connected_app, integration_user, user_agent, job_id, exported_rows, first_query_time, last_delete_time
abiocs.causality_anchor: High-volume Bulk API query on job_id N by the integration token -> deleteJob targeting that same job_id N by the same token, delete-after-query within a 30m window, a query-then-delete sequence outside this identity's learned delete behaviour, anchored to the mass-export event chain.

xql_queries.name: Salesforce Integration Identity Bulk API Baseline Learned
xql_queries.query:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 86400)
| filter cloud_service = "salesforce" and api_type = "Bulk"
| filter operation in ("query", "queryAll")
| comp sum(rows_processed) as baseline_rows, count_distinct(object_name) as baseline_objects by connected_app, integration_user
| filter baseline_rows >= 0
| fields connected_app, integration_user, baseline_rows, baseline_objects

xql_queries.name: Salesforce Bulk API Mass Export with aiohttp Exfil User-Agent
xql_queries.query:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 3600)
| filter cloud_service = "salesforce" and api_type = "Bulk" and operation in ("query", "queryAll")
| filter user_agent = "Python/3.11 aiohttp/3.12.15"
| filter object_name in ("Account", "Contact", "Case", "Opportunity")
| comp sum(rows_processed) as exported_rows, count() as query_jobs by integration_user, connected_app, src_ip
| filter exported_rows >= 1
| sort desc exported_rows
| fields integration_user, connected_app, src_ip, exported_rows, query_jobs

xql_queries.name: Salesforce Bulk API Query-Job Deletion Anti-Forensics Hunt
xql_queries.query:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 86400)
| filter cloud_service = "salesforce" and api_type = "Bulk" and operation = "deleteJob"
| comp count() as deleted_jobs by integration_user, connected_app, user_agent
| filter deleted_jobs >= 1
| sort desc deleted_jobs
| fields integration_user, connected_app, user_agent, deleted_jobs

correlation_rules.name: Post-Consent OAuth Token Abuse — Salesforce Export-Then-Erase Stitch
correlation_rules.logic: ABIOC(Post-Consent OAuth Token High-Volume Bulk API Export Deviating from Integration Baseline) AND ABIOC(Export-Then-Erase Bulk API Query Job Deletion by Exfiltration Token) observed within 30 minutes on the same connected_app and integration_user — fuses the high-volume Bulk API export anomaly and the export-then-erase query-job deletion into a single post-consent OAuth-token-abuse incident anchored to the compromised integration identity (trusted token -> mass CRM export -> job deletion), where no consent, MFA, or interactive login event exists to alert on.

threat_scenarios.name: Post-Consent OAuth Token Abuse Detection via Cortex ABIOC (Salesforce Bulk API)
threat_scenarios.description: Cortex's auto-tuned Analytics Behavioral IOCs learn each Connected App integration identity's Bulk API export baseline and detect post-consent token abuse — high-volume multi-object CRM export followed by export-then-erase query-job deletion — anchored to the integration identity's causality chain, where no consent, MFA, or login event was raised to alert on.

threat_steps.objective: The high-volume Bulk API export deviates from the learned integration baseline and fires the export-deviation ABIOC.
preconditions: Salesforce Event Monitoring ingested into XSIAM.
Integration-identity baseline window elapsed with only low-volume scheduled Bulk API jobs.
steps: Let the integration baseline window elapse.
Drive high-volume Bulk API query jobs across Account/Contact/Case/Opportunity with the exfil user-agent.
success_criteria: ABIOC `Post-Consent OAuth Token High-Volume Bulk API Export Deviating from Integration Baseline` fires.
XQL `Salesforce Bulk API Mass Export with aiohttp Exfil User-Agent` returns >= 1 row.

threat_steps.objective: The query-job deletion following the mass export fires the export-then-erase ABIOC.
preconditions: The export-deviation step (TS-CLOUD-006A) has run for the same integration token.
steps: Issue deleteJob on the Bulk API query jobs created during the export.
success_criteria: ABIOC `Export-Then-Erase Bulk API Query Job Deletion by Exfiltration Token` fires.
XQL `Salesforce Bulk API Query-Job Deletion Anti-Forensics Hunt` returns >= 1 row.

threat_steps.objective: Correlation stitches the export and erase ABIOCs into one post-consent-token-abuse incident.
preconditions: Both ABIOCs fired for the same connected_app + integration_user within the correlation window.
steps: Observe CR-CLOUD-0006 raise one stitched incident.
success_criteria: Correlation `CR-CLOUD-0006` raises exactly one post-consent OAuth-token-abuse incident anchored to the integration identity's causality chain.

preventive_controls: Rotate and tightly scope OAuth access/refresh tokens for third-party Connected Apps, and revoke all active tokens on any Salesloft/Drift-class supply-chain disclosure (Salesloft's own response was to proactively revoke all active access and refresh tokens).
Enforce IP allow-listing / login-range restrictions on Connected App integration users and block Tor exit nodes so a stolen token cannot be replayed from arbitrary infrastructure.
Set per-integration Bulk API row and query-job quotas and alert on any Connected App exceeding its learned export volume or touching object sets outside its normal scope.
detection_engineering: Enable Salesforce Event Monitoring (including UniqueQuery real-time events that log executed SOQL) and Connected App authentication activity, and ingest them into XSIAM so Bulk API query/queryAll/deleteJob operations are modeled and queryable.

Let Cortex auto-tune ABIOCs against each integration identity's learned Bulk API baseline (row volume, object diversity, user-agent) rather than hand-authoring a static rule per object or SOQL string.
Alert on export-then-erase: a Connected App that runs high-volume Bulk API query jobs and then deletes those query jobs within a short window.

Treat the automation user-agent 'Python/3.11 aiohttp/3.12.15' as a high-signal but corroborating IOC; pair it with export volume and Tor-exit-node source IPs, which are high-false-positive for orgs that permit Tor.
